title: Is there really a debris disc around ζ<SUP>2</SUP> Reticuli?
question: Is the double-lobed Herschel/PACS feature around zeta2 Reticuli a real eccentric edge-on debris disc, or background contamination?

data.bands: Band 6 (230 GHz, 1.3 mm) and Band 7 (345 GHz, 870 microns)

what.value: Proper motion 1331.15 mas/yr in RA and 648.52 mas/yr in Dec

evidence.quote: $1331.15 \pm 0.36\,\mathrm{mas/year}$ in Right Ascension and $648.52 \pm 0.43\,\mathrm{mas/year}$ in Declination

what.value: Spectral index 2.6 for debris discs from SED modelling

evidence.quote: the majority of debris discs have a spectral index of 2.6 or smaller (cite: 2017MNRAS.470.3606H)

recipe.method: tclean of combined SPWs, Briggs weighting, primary beam correction

recipe.goal: Test common proper motion of lobes
recipe.method: Compute stellar displacement since Herschel (7.75 yr) from Gaia proper motion and compare with lobe positions
Gaussian ellipse fits deconvolved from beam
Extrapolate SPIRE 250 um flux with spectral index 2.6 assuming uniform surface brightness over 4 (B6) or 6 (B7) beams

evidence.quote: it is expected to have displaced by 11".5 in the North-East direction

not_stated_but_needed: Method of combining the multiple execution blocks
Details of Gaussian fits for lobes
How surface brightness limits were converted from sigma
Herschel/SPIRE 250 um flux used for extrapolation
missing_for_reproduction: Clean parameters beyond robust and cell
score_reason: Simple imaging with key parameters given; detection analysis and limit derivation lack detail.
rediscovery_reason: Data are from a PI project whose proprietary period has likely expired; imaging recipe and numeric flux/limit results are given.
